parts.note: read as pressing clothes in advance, but 'prep' is school slang for the tasks pupils take home after lessons

explanation.surface: Someone does the ironing ahead of time, getting ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ironing' suggests chores around the house; the phrase really points to housework turned school work done at home, with 'Preparatory' hinting at prep.
explanation.definitionFit: At British schools 'prep' (preparation) is the work set for pupils to do outside class, so household-sounding chores done for prep fit.

clue.text: Three bachelors, about mid-January, following Hugh soundly creating a din

indicators.note: following places the bachelors-and-January part after the Hugh sound in the answer
soundly asks for letters that, said out loud, match how the name Hugh is pronounced

parts.note: the name Hugh is pronounced like the letters HU

indicators.note: about means the three bachelors are placed around the middle letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, so three of them give BBB

indicators.note: mid- picks out the central letter of the seven-letter word January

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene caused by three single men and someone named Hugh in the middle of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BBB around U (the middle of January), giving BBUB, which follows HU.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a loud confused noise, so they are synonyms.

parts.note: read as a drawer in a metal cabinet, but 'drawer' here means something that draws or pulls iron towards itself

clue.text: More than just damp clothes to take a dive in

definitions.text: More than just damp clothes to take a dive in

parts.words: More than just damp clothes to take a dive in

explanation.surface: Swimwear for divers is wetter than merely damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' is the step beyond 'damp' and a 'suit' is a set of clothes, so the description names the diver's garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A neoprene diving garment, worn in the sea, is literally clothing that becomes thoroughly soaked.

indicators.note: during means the prayer sits inside the word for the rush, interrupting it

explanation.definitionFit: Both mean remembered or brought back to mind; these are synonyms.

parts.note: reads as someone rushing into view, but also describes a camera lens closing in on a subject

explanation.surface: Something shot rapidly into the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sped along and is also what a camera lens does when it closes in on a subject so it fills the shot.

definitions.meaning: a bishop is in charge of, and so sits above, his diocese, which is called his see
to supervise or manage work done by others

explanation.surface: A question about a bishop's place in managing a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop stands above his diocese (his 'see'), and the verb means to supervise others.

clue.text: There are less of us in it

parts.words: There are less of us in it

explanation.definitionFit: The smaller section of a population, the group with fewer members, is what the speakers belong to.

parts.note: to dock a tail or wage is to cut it short
a yard is a unit of length, a measure

explanation.surface: Cutting back the measurements at a navy base.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipyard where naval vessels are built and repaired is an establishment of the navy.

clue.text: Great, second moment producing display of force

a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A great second moment produces a show of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just a tick' is British slang for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom (from 'speak softly and carry a…') means a threat of power or force.

clue.text: Fox going from marsh to north city area

explanation.surface: A fox travels from a marsh up to an urban district in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode for the City, the financial district.

clue.text: A continental peer found it was not evenly balanced

parts.note: un is French for 'a', so a continental 'a'
a peer is someone of the same standing, an equal

explanation.surface: A European nobleman found the scales were uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' suggests a lord, but here means an equal; 'continental' signals a European language, French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsided or uneven scales are a synonym for lacking balance.

indicators.note: organised means the letters of prayers are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Arranged prayers for a fresh garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' looks like clothing but means a coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting a car again gives it a fresh layer of paint, a new coat.

parts.note: reads as altering one's intentions, but literally means drawing up fresh drawings or blueprints

explanation.definitionFit: Producing fresh drawings or layouts for something literally alters its plans.

clue.text: One having a following in the fashion world

definitions.text: One having a following in the fashion world

parts.words: One having a following in the fashion world
parts.note: a person whose style others copy, with followers in matters of style

explanation.surface: Someone influential in fashion attracts followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who starts a fashion that others copy is a leader with followers in matters of style.

clue.text: During escape that's provided during plane journey

describing meals or entertainment served to passengers in the air

explanation.surface: Something offered while escaping, like a service on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'while fleeing' and 'aboard an aircraft while airborne', as with airline meals.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: Swamping a lone sister with fruit.

explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler does something casually, not professionally, the sense of a non-professional.

explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a bid saying no suit will be trumps is a call.

clue.text: General principle, one applied to the largest numbers

parts.note: a maxim is a general principle or rule of conduct
a is one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: A general rule applied to the biggest figures.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin plural for the greatest values, the highest quantities.

clue.text: Old boy left having objected crazily when cast down

left means departed, so the old boy goes away from the word objected

explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes OB from OBJECTED, leaving JECTED, which 'crazily' rearranges.

parts.note: weighty means serious or grave

indicators.note: turn means the letters of duties and in are turned about into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: To split apart or separate is a synonym for severing.

indicators.note: included means the word he is put inside the word for the right-winger

explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis or conjecture not yet proved is a speculative idea.
